citations.quote: Ethics can be described as a set of moral principles that provide guidance for our behavior; these may be moral principles shared by a community or societal group.
For a profession to be credible, a primary goal is to establish trust among clients and among society in general.
Standard II(A) promotes and maintains a high level of confidence in market integrity, which is one of the foundations of the investment profession.

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: Frames why an ethics framework matters to the investment profession: trust is the mechanism that resolves the principal-agent information asymmetry between investment professionals and clients, and individual ethics breaches have market-level externalities for capital allocation, making the Code and Standards a public good rather than a private moral preference.
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Ethics and Trust in the Investment Profession
